plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the clock mechanism ensures the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the weakly dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value (loss), while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since values are independently drawn and this is a one-shot round, I should bid exactly my value of $27 to ensure optimal outcomes.

This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my own bid only determines when I exit, not what I pay if I win. Therefore, bidding my true value ($31) is the dominant strategy—it maximizes my expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities.

This is effectively a second-price sealed-bid auction (via the ascending clock mechanism), where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids, since you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and pay less than your value, ensuring non-negative profit. Bidding higher risks overpaying; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my true value of $20.
